Documentation folder: T11851-8 (documentation_file)

Revision history: as listed in the table (Initial + 1..10).

Characteristics:
Table 1 (FEW41Y.Z and FEW43Y.Z — reduced bore variants... actually X=1 standard, X=3 advanced; Z=R reduced bore presumably; FEW41/FEW43) and Table 2 (FEW45Y.Z — premium/MC variant).

Common attributes:
- measuring_principle: Electromagnetic
- accuracy_class: 1 and 2
- environmental_class: O (installed outdoors)
- electromagnetic_environment: E2 (Table 1); E1/E2 for Table 2 (transmitter with/without external antenna cable)
- mechanical_class: M1
- temperature_range_ambient: -25/+55 °C
- water_temperature_class: T50 (+0.1/+50 °C)
- maximum_admissible_pressure: 1.6 MPa (16 bar)
- orientation: All positions
- flow_profile_sensitivity_class: U0 and D0 (0×DN upstream/downstream), except DN250+: U3 and D0
- reverse_flow: sensor intended to measure reverse flow
- pressure_loss_class: varies by size and bore type
- power_supply: AC mains 95-240 VAC @ 50/60 Hz; DC 6-32 V; Battery 2×3.6 V (Table 1) or 6×3.6 V (Table 2)
- checking_facilities: Type P permanent automatic checking facility
- software identification: tables 3, 4

Table 2 has the checking facilities row as well; Table 1 has it on page 3 in a separate table (continuation of Table 1).

Now for the model family: This cert covers a big family:
- FEW41Y.Z, FEW43Y.Z, FEW45Y.Z (X=1,3,5)
- Y = 1,2,8,9
- Z = R, V, F
- Sizes DN40 up to DN1800 (reduced bore up to DN600; full bore DN40–DN1800)
- Accuracy class 1 and/or 2
- Power: AC mains vs battery/renewable

The model_level characteristics: The 2-D tables (Tables 5–8) give flow rates per meter size, accuracy class, and power config. These are multi-dimensional: meter size × accuracy class × power configuration (AC mains vs battery). Plus bore type (reduced vs full).

How to structure this? The schema supports:
- model_level: attribute × model matrix
- config_level: attribute × config-axis matrix
- matrix_tables: preserve multi-dim tables

Best approach:
- model_family.models: model_id per meter size? That could be a lot: reduced bore DN40–DN600 (14 sizes) and full bore DN40–DN1800 (~27 sizes). Hmm. Or model_id per (bore type, size). The type designations are FEW (flow sensor) variants and FET (transmitter).

Let me count sizes:
Reduced bore (Z=R): DN40, DN50, DN65, DN80, DN100, DN125, DN150, DN200, DN250, DN300, DN350, DN400, DN450, DN500, DN600 — 15 sizes.
Full bore (Z=F): DN40, DN50, DN65, DN80, DN100, DN125, DN150, DN200, DN250, DN300, DN350, DN400, DN450, DN500, DN600, DN700, DN750, DN800, DN900, DN1000, DN1050, DN1100, DN1200, DN1350, DN1400, DN1500, DN1600, DN1650, DN1800 — 29 sizes.

Virtual full bore (Z=V) also exists in type designation but flow tables don't distinguish V from F ("(Virtual) Full bore" pressure loss combined). Tables 7/8 say "Full bore" — probably includes virtual full bore. The pressure loss section says "(Virtual) Full bore", so tables 7/8 likely cover both V and F.

Given the size, I'll preserve the tables in matrix_tables (Tables 5, 6, 7, 8 for flow rates; Tables 9-12 for indicating device), and populate model_family with model_id = "DN40", ... possibly qualified by bore type, plus config_level entries.

Actually, since the same meter size appears with different values depending on bore type and power config, model_level keyed on just size would conflict. Better: use config_level with axis "power supply" and "bore type"? The config_level shape: {attribute, axis, values: [{condition, value, unit_symbol}]}.

Hmm, but the value differs per (size, class, power config, bore). The cleanest per schema:

- model_family.models: each model_id = meter size (e.g., "DN40"), with attributes including bore_types. But then flow rates differ per config...

Alternative: model_id per size, and config_level entries:
- attribute: minimum_flow_rate_q1, axis: "power_supply_and_accuracy_class" — too messy.

Given rules 4 and 5, I think the practical approach:

1. matrix_tables[]: Tables 5, 6, 7, 8 with rows = {meter_size, accuracy_class, q1_min, q2, q3, q4, ratio_q3_q1} and name indicating bore + power. Also Tables 9-12 for indicating device characteristics.

2. model_family: family_name "AquaMaster4", models with model_id = "FEW41Y.Z", "FEW43Y.Z", "FEW45Y.Z", "FET4*"? Hmm. Actually the type designations FEW41Y.Z etc. are the model identifiers. The X variants: 1=standard, 3=advanced, 5=premium (mobile comms). So FEW41 (standard), FEW43 (advanced), FEW45 (premium/MC). Y = 1,2,8,9. Z = R,V,F.

Actually FEW is the flow sensor; FET is... "FET4*" — likely the transmitter? Hmm, "Type: AquaMaster4 FEW4XY.Z and FET4 \*" — the Y being "integral/remote version, optionally sensor only" suggests FEW covers sensor versions and FET might be the transmitter family. Actually in ABB AquaMaster4: FEW4 = electromagnetic flow sensor (WaterMaster... actually AquaMaster), FET4 = flow... transmitter? AquaMaster4 FET400? Hmm. ABB AquaMaster 3 used FET001/FEW001... In ABB WaterMaster: FEW = flow tube/sensor, FET = flow transmitter electronics. The Y "integral/remote version, optionally sensor only" applies to the combination.

I'll keep it simple: type_designations: ["AquaMaster4 FEW4XY.Z", "FET4*"] with description explaining wildcards.

model_family:
- family_name: "AquaMaster4"
- models: variants based on X: FEW41Y.Z (standard), FEW43Y.Z (advanced), FEW45Y.Z (premium/mobile comms). Plus maybe sensor-only. I'll create model entries:
  - {"model_id": "FEW41Y.Z", "label": "Standard", "attributes": {"wildcard_legend": ...}}
  - {"model_id": "FEW43Y.Z", "label": "Advanced"}
  - {"model_id": "FEW45Y.Z", "label": "Premium (mobile Comms - MC)"}
  Plus FET4 transmitter? Hmm, FET4* is listed as part of the type. I could add {"model_id": "FET4*", "label": "Transmitter"}.

Actually let me reconsider: models[] is "one entry per variant". The main variant axis in tables is meter size × bore × power × class. That's the matrix_tables domain. The FEW41/43/45 are software/characteristic tables domain (Tables 1, 3 vs 2, 4).

I'll do:
- model_family.family_name: "AquaMaster4"
- models: [
  {model_id: "FEW41Y.Z", label: "Standard variant", attributes: {x_code: "1"}},
  {model_id: "FEW43Y.Z", label: "Advanced variant", attributes: {x_code: "3"}},
  {model_id: "FEW45Y.Z", label: "Premium variant (mobile Comms - MC)", attributes: {x_code: "5"}}
]
And note Y/Z codes in family attributes? The schema doesn't have that; maybe add to description.

Alternatively include model entries per meter size. That would be 44 models. That's heavy but follows the R137 example. But the flow tables vary by more than size (class, power). The R137 example had size as model and attributes per size. Here I could make model_id = "DN40 reduced bore" etc. But with class splitting rows... I think matrix_tables is the right primary vessel, with model_level for the size axis maybe not necessary. The rules say populate model_family and model_level for explicit 2-D tables. But this one is 4-D (size × class × bore × power). I'll populate matrix_tables fully and provide config_level for a couple of key axes, plus type_level for the whole-cert attributes.

Let me decide config_level entries:
- attribute: pressure_loss_class — axis "bore_type_and_meter_size": values: [{condition: "reduced bore, DN40-DN50", value: "Δp 40 (0.40 bar)"}, ...]. Values as strings.
- attribute: flow_profile_sensitivity_class — axis "meter_size": [{condition: "DN250 and larger (full bore)", value: "U3 and D0 (3 x DN upstream, 0 x DN downstream)"}, {condition: "all other sizes", value: "U0 and D0"}].
- attribute: battery_configuration: axis "variant": [{condition: "FEW41Y.Z / FEW43Y.Z", value: "2x 3.6 V"}, {condition: "FEW45Y.Z", value: "6x 3.6 V"}].

Power supply characteristics (type_level or config_level):
- ac_mains_voltage: 95–240 V, unit "V" (VAC)
- ac_mains_frequency: 50–60 Hz
- dc_supply_voltage (renewable energy): 6–32 V
- battery: "2x 3.6 V" (FEW41/43) or "6x 3.6 V" (FEW45); battery_operating_range: 2.9–3.6 V.

These differ between Table 1 and Table 2 (battery count, and Table 2 includes batteries in AC/DC). I'll make battery_cells count a config_level attribute or model_level on FEW models.

Water temperature class: T50, range +0.1 to +50 °C.
- water_temperature_class: "T50"
- water_temperature_range: {min: 0.1, max: 50}, °C

Temperature range ambient: {min: -25, max: 55}, °C.

MAP: 1.6 MPa; also 16 bar. I'll record maximum_admissible_pressure: value 1.6, unit "MPa", footnote none. Could add alternative: value 16 bar. I'll do one characteristic with unit MPa, maybe mention bar in another entry "maximum_admissible_pressure_alt": skip; keep just MPa. Actually maybe record both as two entries: pressure 1.6 MPa. Fine.
